plain: To doubt or mistrust; to think something may be so without proof

webster.text: To mistrust; to imagine or have a slight opinion that something exists, but without proof and often upon weak evidence or no evidence at all.

example.quote: Our constituents do not suspect our delegates to the state legislature, but we suspect the members of the future Congress.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 6, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
